newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel chief departs before talks with Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel chief departs before talks with Mobutu.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila left his headquarters in southeastern Zaire on Thursday to visit some neighbouring countries before his first face-to-face meeting with President Mobutu Sese Seko on Friday.
Officials said Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, would travel to some of Zaire's neighbours before flying to South Africa and on to the talks.

Kabila told Reuters late on Wednesday that the talks brokered by South African President Nelson Mandela, planned to take place on a South African navy ship, would only discuss the departure from power of Mobutu, Zaire's ruler for 32 years.
"The talks will just be about Mobutu and what we do with him. Our uncompromising demand is that he leaves power and we shall look after him," Kabila said.

Kabila spoke as his rebel army advanced towards the town of Kenge on the route to the capital Kinshasa, where the rebel chief said Mobutu's army had begun blowing up bridges to try to fend off the advance.
